title: Annual water quality report 2025
summary: The annual consumer confidence report, summarized: no story violations, lead/copper below action levels, and what changed after the new filters.
body:
This is the story version of the report mailed each June. In 2025 the district ran 1,140 compliance samples (story count) across the plant, tanks and 42 tap sites.

Two things changed: granular activated carbon cut taste-and-odor complaints by half in the story data, and a corrosion-control tweak nudged pH from 6.9 to 7.1 to protect household plumbing.

Reading the table

Key results at right are the numbers residents ask about. Full lab tables would be attachments in a real district; here the summary is the point.
key_results: pH 7.1 avg · Chlorine 0.8 mg/L · Turbidity 0.08 NTU · Lead 90th %ile 4 ppb (action 15) · Copper 0.21 ppm (action 1.3) — all story figures

title: Q3 2026 quality snapshot: a muddy river, clear taps
summary: Storm turbidity, extra chlorine monitoring in the heat, and PFAS screening results — the quarter in four paragraphs.
body:
July heat raised chlorine demand; operators shortened tank turnover (story). The early-October storm is covered in the resolved alert and in the turbidity line here.

Voluntary PFAS screening (story) came back below the reporting limit at the plant tap; the district repeats it yearly because residents asked, not because a rule required it in the story.
key_results: Turbidity max 0.21 NTU during storm week · Chlorine residual never below 0.4 mg/L · PFAS below reporting limit (story)

title: Lead and copper: what Carrow Bend found at kitchen taps
summary: How tap sampling actually works, why first-draw samples sit overnight, and the three story homes where the district helped replace a service line.
body:
Lead rarely comes from the river or the plant — it comes from older household plumbing. That is why sampling happens at kitchen taps in homes built before the story cutoff year.

Three homes exceeded the story guide value (not the district system result); each traced to a galvanized interior line, and the district's story cost-share replaced two.
key_results: System 90th percentile lead 4 ppb vs 15 ppb action level (story) · 3 homes individually higher, all plumbing-related in the story
